name: Kubernetes AI Deployment
certifications: NVIDIA-Certified Associate: AI Infrastructure and Operations (NCA-AIIO)

beginner.summary: For engineers who already deploy ordinary applications on Kubernetes and now have to run GPU-backed AI workloads. Covers how a GPU node is assembled (driver, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, CDI), installing the NVIDIA GPU Operator, requesting GPUs, building model-server images, getting model weights into pods, serving an LLM with vLLM and with KServe, sizing GPU memory for weights and KV cache, probes for slow-loading models, batch inference and a single-GPU fine-tuning Job, GPU and token-level metrics, autoscaling with HPA and KEDA, GPU time-slicing, and fault diagnosis, ending with a production-ready single-node LLM endpoint.
prerequisites: Deploys and debugs Deployments, Services, Jobs, PersistentVolumeClaims and Secrets with kubectl, and installs charts with Helm
Knows what a large language model, model weights and an inference API are, and can call an HTTP API with curl or Python

Has access to a Kubernetes 1.33 or later cluster with at least one NVIDIA GPU node (for example an L4, L40S or A100), either a managed cluster on EKS, GKE or AKS or a lab cluster provided by the trainer
outcomes: Prepare GPU nodes with the NVIDIA GPU Operator and schedule pods that request whole or time-sliced GPUs
Serve an open-weight LLM through vLLM and KServe with correct probes, memory settings and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Run batch inference and a single-GPU fine-tuning Job that store results and checkpoints on persistent storage
Monitor GPU and token metrics with DCGM Exporter and Prometheus, autoscale on serving metrics, and diagnose the common GPU pod failures
